keyword: how do astronauts go to the bathroom in space

verifications.claim: Astronauts in space use specialized vacuum toilets that utilize airflow instead of gravity to collect waste.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: In the absence of weight, the collection and retention of liquid and solid waste is directed by use of airflow. (R1); specially designed vacuum toilet... suction (R3,R4,R6,R7); space toilets use air flow to pull urine and feces away from the body (R5)
verifications.reasoning: Directly stated across multiple sources that airflow/suction/vacuum replaces gravity.

verifications.claim: A funnel-and-hose system collects waste for urination.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: specially shaped funnel and hose for urine (R1,R5); hose with a funnel at the end for peeing (R3,R4,R6,R7); use a hose to dispose of urine (R2)
verifications.reasoning: Explicitly described as funnel-and-hose for urine collection.

verifications.claim: A seat with suction collects solid waste.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: the seat for bowel movements (R1,R5); small raised toilet seat for pooping... suctioning as soon as the lid is lifted (R3,R4,R6,R7)
verifications.reasoning: Seat with suction explicitly for solid waste.

verifications.claim: Liquid waste is often recycled into drinking water.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: recycle pee... turned back into clean, drinkable water (R3,R4,R6,R7); recycles water for further use... astronauts do drink after it is filtered (R5); ISS urine processed (R1 context)
verifications.reasoning: Direct support for urine recycling into drinking water on ISS.

verifications.claim: Solid waste is stored and incinerated upon re-entry.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: loaded into a cargo ship that burns up on re-entry (R1); burned up in the atmosphere... flaming astronaut poo (R3,R4,R6,R7)
verifications.reasoning: Solid waste stored then burned/incinerated on re-entry.

verifications.claim: Astronauts use leg restraints, foot pads, or handholds to keep themselves positioned on the toilet because of microgravity.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: foot restraints and handholds... traditional thigh straps (leg restraints) were a hassle (R1,R5); handholds and footholds (foot pads) (R3,R4,R6,R7)
verifications.reasoning: Direct mentions of handholds, foot restraints/footholds, thigh straps (leg restraints) for positioning in microgravity.

verifications.claim: Astronauts sit on a small seat that creates a seal to ensure no waste escapes.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: small and pointy... ideal body contact to make sure that everything goes where it should (R1,R5); tight fit between the toilet seat and the astronauts’ behinds, the toilet seat is smaller (R3,R4,R6,R7)
verifications.reasoning: Small seat provides seal/tight contact to prevent escape.

verifications.claim: Solid waste is collected in bags.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: solid-waste collection bags... individual water-tight bags (R1,R5); vacuumed into garbage bags (R3,R4,R6,R7)

verifications.claim: Solid waste bags are placed into a storage container.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: compacted in a removable fecal storage canister (R1); put into airtight containers (R3,R4,R6,R7)

verifications.claim: Astronauts use a hose with a specialized funnel for urination.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: hose... attached to the vacuum chamber... detachable urine receptacle... plastic funnel (R1); hose with a funnel (R3 etc.); specially shaped funnel and hose (R5)

verifications.claim: The specialized funnel for urination can be used by both men and women while standing or sitting.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: different versions for male and female... can be used simultaneously (R1); sit or stand... hold the funnel and hose tightly (R3 etc., for both); funnel... reflecting feedback from female astronauts (R5)
verifications.reasoning: Funnels adapted for both genders, usable sitting/standing.

verifications.claim: Solid waste containers are emptied periodically.
verifications.label: VAGUE
verifications.evidence: Full containers are transferred to Progress for disposal (R1)
verifications.reasoning: Containers transferred when full, implying periodic emptying, but not explicitly 'periodically'.

verifications.claim: Solid waste is eventually burned up in the atmosphere with other trash.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: burns up on re-entry through Earth's atmosphere... with other trash (R1); burned up in the atmosphere with the spacecraft (R3 etc.)

verifications.claim: The ISS uses a system to turn urine into purified drinkable water.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: All astronaut pee is collected and turned back into clean, drinkable water (R3 etc.); recycle about 90%... including urine (R5)

verifications.claim: Astronauts wear a diaper known as the Maximum Absorbency Garment (MAG) during long spacewalks.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: Maximum Absorbency Garment

verifications.claim: NASA recently upgraded to the $23 million Universal Waste Management System (UWMS).
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: A $23 million next-generation space toilet called the Universal Waste Management System (UWMS) (R1); NASA spent $23 million on a new and improved toilet... Universal Waste Management System (R3 etc.)

verifications.claim: The UWMS is smaller.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: 65% smaller... more compact (R1,R5)

verifications.claim: The UWMS is more efficient.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: Improved Efficiency... more reliable (title and text R5)

verifications.claim: The UWMS is more comfortable.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: more comfortable (R3 etc.); More Comfort (R5 title)

verifications.claim: The UWMS is specifically designed to better accommodate female astronauts.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: first space toilet designed specifically for women as well as men (R1); reflecting feedback from female astronauts (R5)
